chunks: From him, from Ṣafwān, from Ibn Muskān, from al-Ḥalabī, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about wiping over the khuffs,
So he said: “Do not wipe.” And he said: “Indeed, my grandfather said: The Book has preceded the khuffs.”

key_terms.جَدِّي: my grandfather, referring to an earlier Imam or the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم in the line of transmission
key_terms.لَا تَمْسَحْ: do not wipe; a direct prohibition
key_terms.ٱلْخُفَّيْنِ: the two leather socks or footwear over which wiping is being discussed
key_terms.ٱلْكِتَابُ: the Book, meaning the Quran as the primary textual authority
key_terms.ٱلْمَسْحِ: wiping, specifically in the context of ritual purification

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام say about wiping over khuffs in wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning wudu (ablution), forbidding wiping over the khuffs. The statement that “the Book has preceded the khuffs” indicates that the Quranic rule regarding wudu (ablution) takes priority over this practice.
